items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: You ask everybody what happened to Dink... Dink wasn't his name. That was a nickname. And I asked for his name

ctx.x: And did he continue on after he left you?

Yes, he did, but I don't know what ever happened to him. Nobody else knows. You ask everybody what happened to Dink, and nobody can tell you. Dink wasn't his name. That was a nickname. And I asked for his name, and I couldn't tell you to save my life.
I think I found it somewhere. I know Herbert Hall has gone on with Eddie Condon.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Dink, we actually rehearsed most every day.

ctx.x: There's an interlude and he brought Billy Douglas in there. No, Dink Taylor came after the interlude, if I remember.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: Billy Douglas and Dink Taylor, man. They would turn that shirt around. Now those two, they were characters... when we were playing in St. Petersburg, Florida... Dink Taylor had to sell him...

ctx.x: Yeah, I see. Now did anybody, when they had a dirty shirt, would anybody ever do a thing with wearing the shirts inside and out?

Yes. Billy Douglas and Dink Taylor, man. They would turn that shirt around. Now those two, they were characters. I found this so funny. Yeah, my wife possibly told you that. Oh yes, she did. Sure she did.
Now this Judge Sondas who made the decision with Sandoz, how do you spell his name?
